Honors Physics Lecture Outlines

Lecture 1: Electromagnetism (Chapter 8)

Learning Objectives

  • Understand the relationship between electricity and magnetism
  • Apply right-hand rules to determine magnetic field directions
  • Calculate magnetic forces on moving charges and current-carrying conductors
  • Explain electromagnetic induction and its applications

I. Introduction to Electromagnetism

  • Historical context: Oersted’s experiment
  • Unification of electric and magnetic phenomena
  • Overview of electromagnetic applications in modern technology

II. Magnetic Fields and Forces

  • A. Magnetic Field Concepts
    • Definition and units (Tesla)
    • Visualization techniques
    • Field patterns around different magnetic sources
  • B. Right-Hand Rules
    • Current-carrying wire rule
    • Solenoid rule
    • Force on moving charge rule
  • C. Magnetic Force Calculations
    • Force on moving charges: F = qvB sinθ
    • Force on current-carrying conductors: F = ILB sinθ
    • Applications: mass spectrometers and cyclotrons

III. Electromagnetic Induction

  • A. Faraday’s Law
    • Induced EMF and changing magnetic flux
    • Mathematical representation: ε = -N(ΔΦ/Δt)
    • Factors affecting induced EMF
  • B. Lenz’s Law
    • Direction of induced current
    • Conservation of energy implications
    • Demonstration: falling magnet through copper tube
  • C. Applications
    • Generators: converting mechanical to electrical energy
    • Motors: converting electrical to mechanical energy
    • Transformers and power transmission

IV. Class Demonstrations

  • Interactive simulation of field lines
  • Hand-cranked generator demonstration
  • Electromagnetic induction with solenoids and galvanometer

V. Assessment Activity

  • Concept mapping: Connecting magnetic field concepts with induction
  • Problem-solving: Calculating forces and induced EMF
  • Quick-write: Real-world applications of electromagnetic principles

Lecture 2: Electricity (Chapter 9)

Learning Objectives

  • Apply Coulomb’s law to calculate electric forces
  • Analyze electric fields and their effects
  • Understand electric potential and potential energy concepts
  • Solve circuit problems using Ohm’s law and Kirchhoff’s laws

I. Electric Forces and Fields

  • A. Coulomb’s Law
    • Electric charge properties
    • Force calculation: F = kq₁q₂/r²
    • Comparison with gravitational force
  • B. Electric Fields
    • Definition and units (N/C)
    • Field calculations for point charges and charge distributions
    • Field visualization and mapping
  • C. Electric Potential
    • Electric potential energy vs. electric potential
    • Potential due to point charges
    • Equipotential surfaces
    • Capacitors and dielectrics

II. Electric Circuits

  • A. Current and Resistance
    • Electric current: definition and units
    • Resistance and Ohm’s law: V = IR
    • Resistivity and temperature effects
  • B. Circuit Analysis
    • Series and parallel connections
    • Kirchhoff’s voltage law
    • Kirchhoff’s current law
    • Solving complex circuit problems
  • C. Circuit Components
    • RC circuits and time constants
    • Power in electric circuits: P = IV
    • Energy transfer and conservation

III. Class Demonstrations

  • Van de Graaff generator for electrostatic principles
  • Circuit building demonstration with multimeter readings
  • RC circuit charging/discharging with oscilloscope

IV. Assessment Activity

  • Circuit design challenge
  • Electric field mapping exercise
  • Numerical problem set: Calculating currents, voltages, and resistances

Lecture 3: Optics (Chapter 10)

Learning Objectives

  • Differentiate between geometric and wave optics
  • Apply the laws of reflection and ray diagrams
  • Understand wave phenomena including interference and diffraction
  • Connect optics to the broader electromagnetic spectrum

I. Geometric Optics

  • A. Nature of Light
    • Wave-particle duality overview
    • Speed of light and refractive index
    • History of optics development
  • B. Reflection
    • Law of reflection
    • Plane mirrors and image formation
    • Virtual vs. real images
  • C. Curved Mirrors
    • Concave and convex mirrors
    • Ray diagrams and image characteristics
    • Mirror equation and magnification

II. Wave Optics

  • A. Interference
    • Principle of superposition
    • Young’s double-slit experiment
    • Constructive and destructive interference
    • Applications of interference
  • B. Diffraction
    • Single-slit diffraction pattern
    • Diffraction gratings
    • Resolution limits and applications
  • C. Polarization
    • Linear, circular, and elliptical polarization
    • Polarization by reflection
    • Applications in technology and daily life

III. Connecting to Electromagnetism

  • The electromagnetic spectrum
  • Light as electromagnetic waves
  • Maxwell’s predictions and Hertz’s confirmation

IV. Class Demonstrations

  • Laser interference and diffraction patterns
  • Polarization with polarizing filters
  • Optical illusions and mirages explained

V. Assessment Activity

  • Ray diagram drawing exercise
  • Wave phenomena identification quiz
  • Application brainstorming: Modern uses of optical principles
